docs.title: Client entertainment and business meals
docs.summary: When client dinners and business meals are reimbursable, limits per person, attendee rules.
docs.body: Business meals with clients or prospects are reimbursable when they have a clear business purpose. Itemize every meal: list each attendee, their company and the topic discussed. The limit is USD 120 per person including tax and tip; amounts above the limit need written VP approval before the event. Alcohol is reimbursable only as part of a client meal and never for internal team events. Employee-only team dinners are paid from the team morale budget, not as client entertainment. Use the expense category client_entertainment and attach the itemized receipt, not just the card slip. Meals with government officials require Legal pre-approval regardless of amount. Submit within 30 days.

docs.title: Travel booking policy
docs.summary: How to book flights, hotels and rail; class of travel; booking channel.
docs.body: Book all flights, hotels and rental cars through the TravelDesk portal so duty-of-care tracking works. Economy is standard; premium economy is allowed on flights over 6 hours and business class only on flights over 10 hours or with an approved medical accommodation. Prefer rail for trips under 4 hours door to door. Hotels must be within the nightly city cap shown in TravelDesk; stays above the cap need a justification in the booking notes. Book at least 14 days ahead where possible; last-minute bookings are reviewed monthly by Finance. Personal travel combined with business travel is allowed if the extra cost is paid personally.

docs.title: Per diem rates
docs.summary: Daily meal allowance amounts for domestic and international travel.
docs.body: Travelers receive a daily per diem for meals, snacks and tips instead of itemizing meals. Domestic per diem: USD 65 per full travel day. International per diem: USD 105 per full travel day, or the Finance-published city rate for high-cost cities such as London, Tokyo, Zurich and New York. First and last travel days are paid at 75 percent. Meals provided by a conference, hotel or client reduce the per diem: breakfast 15 percent, lunch 25 percent, dinner 40 percent. Per diem cannot be claimed for local events within 50 km of your home office.

docs.title: Procurement approval thresholds
docs.summary: Who approves a purchase request based on its total value; competitive bids.
docs.body: Every purchase over USD 1,000 needs a purchase request before any commitment to a vendor. Approval is routed by total value: up to USD 5,000 the direct manager approves; from USD 5,000 to USD 25,000 the department VP approves; above USD 25,000 the CFO approves and three competitive bids are required. Hardware requests for standard laptops and monitors go through IT first so they use the standard catalog. Splitting one purchase into several smaller requests to avoid a threshold is a policy violation and is detected automatically by the procurement system.

docs.title: Vendor onboarding
docs.summary: Steps and documents needed to add a new vendor before the first order.
docs.body: New vendors must be onboarded before the first purchase order is issued. Submit the vendor's legal name, tax ID, bank details and a completed security questionnaire through the procurement system. Vendors that will store or process Restricted data also need a Security review and a signed data processing agreement. Onboarding normally takes 10 business days; urgent onboarding requires VP sponsorship. Prefer existing preferred vendors whenever they can meet the need, because they already have negotiated pricing and completed due diligence.

docs.title: Paid time off (PTO)
docs.summary: PTO accrual, requesting time off, carryover and payout rules.
docs.body: Full-time employees accrue 1.75 days of PTO per month (21 days per year), rising to 25 days after five years of service. Request time off in the HR system at least two weeks ahead for absences of three days or more. Up to 5 unused days carry over to the next year and must be used by March 31; anything above 5 days is forfeited on January 1. The HR system shows the live remaining balance, which already subtracts approved and pending requests; payroll accrual reports show days earned, not days remaining. Unused PTO is paid out at termination only where law requires.

docs.title: Parental leave
docs.summary: Paid leave for birth, adoptive and foster parents; notice and timing.
docs.body: Birth parents receive 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave; non-birth, adoptive and foster parents receive 12 weeks. Leave must be taken within 12 months of the birth or placement and can be split into two blocks. Give HR at least 30 days notice where possible. Benefits continue during leave, and PTO keeps accruing. A phased return of up to four weeks at 60 percent schedule with full pay is available after parental leave.

docs.title: Remote and hybrid work
docs.summary: Eligibility for remote work, core hours, home office stipend, working abroad.
docs.body: Most roles are hybrid with two anchor days per week in the office. Fully remote work needs manager and HR approval and is reviewed yearly. Everyone must be available during core hours from 10:00 to 15:00 local time. Remote and hybrid employees get a one-time USD 500 home office stipend; fully remote employees also receive a USD 40 monthly internet allowance. Working from another country needs HR and Legal approval and is capped at 20 working days per year.

docs.title: Password and MFA standard
docs.summary: Passphrase rules, multi-factor authentication, credential sharing.
docs.body: Use a unique passphrase of at least 14 characters for single sign-on. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule but must be changed immediately if exposure is suspected. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for email, VPN, source code, finance systems and any system with customer data; administrators must use hardware security keys. IT will never ask for your password. Self-service password reset is available from the sign-in page; account unlocks after repeated failed attempts happen automatically after 30 minutes or through the IT service desk.

docs.title: VPN access standard
docs.summary: Who gets VPN, certificate-based profiles, resets and revocation.
docs.body: VPN access uses per-device certificates issued by IT; shared VPN profiles are prohibited. A VPN reset revokes the old certificate and issues a new profile to the user's verified company email, typically within 5 minutes. Resets are allowed for the user themselves or by IT on a ticket from the user's manager. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to Security first so the certificate is revoked immediately. VPN sessions disconnect after 12 hours and require MFA on every connection.

docs.title: Software request process
docs.summary: How to request new software, licenses and browser extensions.
docs.body: Request software through the IT portal with a business justification. IT checks whether an approved alternative already exists, confirms single sign-on support and reviews data handling before purchase. Free tools and browser extensions that access company data need the same review. Standard catalog software is installed automatically within one business day of approval. Licenses unused for 90 days are reclaimed.

docs.title: Hardware refresh standard
docs.summary: Laptop and peripheral entitlements, refresh cycle, standard models.
docs.body: Employees receive a standard laptop from the IT catalog: a 14-inch business laptop for most roles and a high-performance model for engineering and data roles. Laptops are refreshed every 36 months or earlier if they fail. Standard peripherals (monitor, dock, headset) are provided on request. Non-standard hardware requires manager approval and a purchase request. Returned devices are wiped and recycled through the certified e-waste partner.

docs.title: Meeting room booking rules
docs.summary: How to book rooms, capacity rules, no-show release, recurring bookings.
docs.body: Book meeting rooms through the facilities system or the calendar add-in. Choose a room whose capacity is at least the number of attendees but no more than double it, so large rooms stay available. Bookings are released automatically if nobody checks in within 10 minutes of the start time. Recurring bookings expire after 3 months and must be renewed. Rooms with video conferencing are prioritized for meetings with remote participants. Building B rooms on floor 3 are reserved for customer meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

docs.title: Building access and hours
docs.summary: Opening hours, badge access, visitors and after-hours rules.
docs.body: Buildings A and B are open from 07:00 to 20:00 on weekdays; badge access is available 24/7 for employees. Visitors must be registered in advance and escorted at all times. After-hours work alone in labs is not allowed. Lost badges must be reported to Security the same day; a replacement badge is issued at reception after identity verification.

docs.title: Parking policy
docs.summary: Requesting parking spaces, EV charging and accessible parking.
docs.body: Parking spaces are limited and allocated per day through the facilities system. Requests open 7 days in advance. EV charging bays are limited to 4 hours per day. Accessible parking is reserved for badge holders with an accessibility permit. Car-pooling employees get priority on Mondays and Fridays.

docs.title: Sales discount approval matrix
docs.summary: Which discounts sales reps can give and who approves larger discounts.
docs.body: Account executives may discount up to 10 percent on list price. Discounts from 10 to 20 percent need regional sales director approval; above 20 percent require the CRO and Finance. Multi-year prepaid deals may receive an extra 5 percent. Quotes must be generated in the CRM so approvals are recorded; manual PDF quotes are not valid.

docs.title: CRM data hygiene
docs.summary: Rules for keeping accounts, contacts and opportunities accurate.
docs.body: Log every customer meeting and call in the CRM within 24 hours. Opportunities must have a close date, amount and next step; stale opportunities older than 90 days without activity are flagged weekly. Duplicate accounts must be merged rather than deleted. Personal data of contacts is limited to business contact details.

docs.title: NDA and contract review
docs.summary: When to use the NDA template and how to send contracts to Legal.
docs.body: Use the standard mutual NDA for discussions with prospects and partners; one-way NDAs only when we disclose but do not receive confidential information. Any edits to the template require Legal review. All customer, vendor and partner contracts must be reviewed by Legal before signature; allow 5 business days. Only authorized signatories may sign contracts on behalf of the company.

docs.title: Data classification
docs.summary: Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted data handling.
docs.body: Company data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted. Customer personal data and payment data are Restricted and may never be stored on personal devices, sent to personal email or pasted into unapproved AI tools. Confidential and Restricted files can be shared externally only through the secure file transfer service. Data owners review classification yearly.

docs.title: Security incident reporting
docs.summary: What counts as an incident and how fast to report it to the SOC.
docs.body: Report any suspected security incident to the Security Operations Center within 1 hour: lost or stolen devices, phishing emails you clicked, malware alerts, or data sent to the wrong recipient. Call extension 4400 or email the SOC. Do not investigate on your own and do not delete suspicious emails; use the Report Phishing button so they can be analyzed.
